headline: The frame, the money module and the six looks hold up well. Money has teeth, tokens match the design source in all twelve combinations, axe is clean, and production is pinned with no dev tools showing. Three Majors to fix first: an unknown screen id crashes to the router's default error page, a real touch long-press on Scan picks the sheet row under the finger, and the no-float lint leaves Number() unguarded outside files named money*.

findings.title: An unknown screen id crashes the app to TanStack's default 'Something went wrong!' page, with no tab bar and no way back
findings.detail: `/s/<id>` with an id not in the registry renders TanStack Router's built-in error component. `AnyScreen` throws `redirect()` from inside a component render (router.tsx), which the router treats as a render error, not a redirect. The root route has no `errorComponent` or `notFoundComponent`, so any later screen that throws, and any stale or mistyped deep link, lands on this dead end. It's the same in the production build. An unknown top-level path (`/nope`) shows a bare 'Not Found'. Neither follows patterns.md §7 *Error*: what happened, what to do next, and a button that does it, inside the frame. B01 is the frame every later slice builds on (brief: nothing here may be a stand-in).
findings.repro: Open http://localhost:4173/s/does-not-exist (or the production build at :4176). Also try /nope and /s/..%2F..%2Fetc.

findings.title: Scan's long-press with a real touch: lifting the finger picks the sheet row that appeared under it
findings.detail: With touch events driven through Chromium's own input pipeline (CDP `Input.dispatchTouchEvent`), holding Scan for 650 ms opens *Add a payment* at 500 ms. On release, Chromium synthesises the click at the finger's position, which is now the sheet's *From gallery* row, so the app navigates straight to `/s/crop`. `useLongPress` swallows only the click on the Scan button itself (`fired`), not a click that lands on the new sheet. The slice's own test drives the long-press with `page.mouse`, where mousedown and mouseup hit different elements and no click fires, so it can't see this. On a phone, Chromium's own long-press gesture may suppress the click when the system's touch-and-hold delay is 500 ms or less. With *Medium* or *Long* (1 s, 1.5 s, a common accessibility setting, also on Xiaomi), a 600–900 ms hold is a tap to Chromium but a long-press to the app. Phone check queued in docs/local.md.

findings.title: The no-float lint bans Number() and unary + only in files named money*, so a block that renders amounts can parse typed text through a float unnoticed
findings.detail: eslint.config.js applies the `Number(…)`, unary `+` and `parseInt` bans only to `MONEY_FILES` (`**/money*`, `**/*Money*` and similar globs). `parseFloat` and `toFixed` are banned everywhere, but `Math.round(Number(typed) * 100)` or `+typed * 100` in `rows.tsx`, `detail.tsx` or `hero.tsx` (all of which render amounts) passes lint and the no-float test suite. Later slices will parse amounts in files named for their screen (`confirm.tsx`, `manual.tsx`, `split.tsx`), outside the guard. CLAUDE.md: `0.1 + 0.2` must be impossible anywhere money flows. Nothing in the current code does this. The guard has a hole.
findings.repro: Append `export const plantedSen = (typed: string) => Math.round(Number(typed) * 100);` and `export const plantedSen2 = (typed: string) => Math.round(+typed * 100);` to apps/web/src/blocks/rows.tsx, detail.tsx and hero.tsx; run `npx eslint` on them and `npx vitest run scripts`; then `git checkout -- apps/web/src/blocks`.

findings.title: Switching look flips data-look before the look's module arrives: the tab bar breaks while it loads, and stays broken if the load fails
findings.detail: `applyTheme` sets `<html data-look>` at once, while `LookProvider` keeps the previous look's drawing until the new module arrives. In between, the old look's tab bar is laid out under the new look's CSS, and the bar grows from 79 px to 134 px with *More* wrapped to a second row. Offline (no service worker until B02), the chunk never arrives, `loadLook` has no `catch`, and the broken frame stays until reload. This matters for B14's reveal and any look change on a weak connection.

findings.title: The hygiene check misses a denylisted string in a file path, and one left in an earlier commit of the PR
findings.detail: scripts/hygiene.mjs uses `git grep` on the working tree, so it reads file contents at HEAD only. A denylisted employer name used as a folder name passes, and so does one committed and then deleted later in the same PR. The second stays in history if the PR is merged with its commits. CI checks out with the default depth and doesn't scan the PR's commits.

findings.title: The gallery and the dev panel ship in the production build, and any build that isn't explicitly production gets the dev tools
findings.detail: router.tsx lazy-imports `./dev/gallery` without the `DEV_TOOLS` gate, and the gallery imports `./dev-panel`, so `gallery-*.js` (398 kB) and `dev-panel-*.js` are emitted into the production build and referenced from its entry chunk. Neither is loaded or shown: the gallery route redirects and nothing fetches them, which FLOW-8 confirms. But anyone can fetch them from /assets/. vite.config.ts treats any build without `VERCEL_ENV=production` or `SEN_ENV=production` as a preview with the dev tools. A build made elsewhere (B02's bundled-app option, or a manual deploy) fails open.
findings.repro: `SEN_ENV=production pnpm exec vite build --outDir <dir>`; ls <dir>/assets | grep -E 'gallery|dev'; then GET /assets/gallery-*.js from the production preview.

findings.title: The DIR objects carry no tokens, extra or fonts
findings.detail: patterns.md §1 and the brief list `tokens`, `extra` and `fonts` on each look's `DIR`. `packages/looks/src/types.ts` has `radius`, `icons`, `icon`, `wordmark`, `heroFigure`, `strip`, `avatar`, `tabs` and `reveal: null`, but no `tokens`, `extra` or `fonts`. The values do reach the app, through `looks.gen.css` from each look's theme.css (FLOW-1 matched every token in all twelve combinations). Native pieces that need a look's colours (notifications, widgets, the island, D77 and D101) will have no TypeScript object to read. Record the choice as a decision, or add the fields.

findings.title: Gaps in the slice's own tests (what they claim against what they exercise)
findings.detail: (1) *WebGL fallback* is exercised through a `?gl=0` dev flag, not a browser without WebGL. QA ran Chromium with `--disable-webgl --disable-3d-apis`, and both fallbacks drew (ink 4555 and 4286). (2) *The avatar plays its eight states* checks only that each canvas is non-empty, never that the states differ. QA confirmed eight distinct drawings per look. (3) The long-press is driven by mouse only, which hides finding 2. (4) The 1.5× test asserts the `--text-scale` variable. QA confirmed text really grows (16 → 24 px). (5) No e2e drives a badge of 0.

findings.title: parseSen trims every kind of whitespace, including a newline and a no-break space
findings.detail: `input.trim()` makes `"12.5\n"` → 1250 and `"12\u00a0"` → 1200. That's documented ("Spaces around the text are ignored") and safe, since no float is involved and the value is right. Recorded because the brief says anything beyond the listed forms is rejected.
